roles.title: German-Speaking Customer Support Representative
roles.overview: Customer support specialists are often the first point of contact for customers who need clear, timely help with a product or service. In this type of role, you would answer enquiries from German-speaking customers, investigate problems and make sure each interaction ends with an understandable next step. Opportunities may arise with technology companies, subscription businesses, online marketplaces and international service teams based in Ireland. German proficiency matters because customers expect precise explanations and a natural, reassuring experience in their own language. English is equally useful for collaborating with colleagues in product, billing, operations and engineering. Depending on the organisation, the work may involve phone, email, live chat or a combination of channels. Strong performers can build expertise in complex cases, quality assurance and customer experience improvement. Over time, the role can provide a route into team leadership, customer success, operations or training. The exact channels, hours and responsibilities depend on the employer and any confirmed vacancy.
responsibilities: Respond to German-language enquiries through the support channels used by the employer.
Investigate account, billing or product issues and explain practical resolutions.
Record accurate case notes and outcomes in a customer support platform.
Escalate technical or sensitive cases using agreed procedures and response times.
Identify recurring questions and contribute to knowledge-base improvements.
Coordinate with billing, product and operations colleagues when cases cross teams.
Maintain service quality, confidentiality and appropriate handling of customer data.
essential: Professional German fluency, normally C1 or equivalent practical ability.
Good written and spoken English for internal collaboration.
Clear communication, patience and sound problem-solving skills.
Ability to organise multiple enquiries and follow defined processes.
Comfort using digital tools and learning new support systems.

Previous customer-facing, retail, hospitality or contact-centre experience.

roles.title: German-Speaking Sales Development Representative (SDR/BDR)
roles.overview: Sales development is a common entry point into business-to-business technology sales. A German-speaking SDR or BDR researches prospective customers, starts commercial conversations and helps an account executive understand which organisations could benefit from a product or service. In Ireland, these teams often support Germany, Austria and Switzerland from an international sales hub. Strong German skills help you approach decision-makers credibly, handle objections and understand differences in local business expectations. English is typically used for internal coaching, pipeline reviews and collaboration with marketing and sales operations. The work can combine structured outbound prospecting with qualification of inbound enquiries, and success is usually measured through activity quality and qualified opportunities rather than signed contracts alone. This career path can suit someone who enjoys research, communication and measurable progress. With experience, opportunities may include senior SDR roles, account executive positions, sales enablement or revenue operations. Targets, tools, territory and compensation structure vary by employer.

roles.title: German-Speaking KYC / Compliance Analyst
roles.overview: KYC and compliance analysts support financial institutions and regulated businesses in understanding customers, verifying information and identifying potential financial-crime risks. A German-speaking analyst may review customer documentation or communicate with counterparties in Germany, Austria and Switzerland while working with a compliance or operations team in Ireland. German fluency is useful for interpreting records and obtaining clear information; English is generally required for internal policies, case documentation and escalation. The role may involve customer due diligence, beneficial ownership checks, screening alerts, periodic reviews or remediation work. Analysts must distinguish routine information gaps from cases requiring specialist review and follow documented procedures rather than make unsupported assumptions. Depending on the employer, work may be subject to financial-services regulation, audit requirements and strict information-security controls. Experience can lead to enhanced due diligence, AML investigations, sanctions operations, compliance advisory or team leadership. The applicable regulatory framework, systems and decision-making authority depend on the hiring entity.

Protect sensitive records and comply with access-control requirements.
